newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - March 10.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - March 10.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING AND MARKETING:

NEW YORK - Omnicom's BBDO advertising agency has dropped out of the chase for the $90 million Delta Air Lines ad account, ending 51 years of association with the Atlanta-based airline. The remaining finalists for the account are Interpublic's Ammirati Puris Lintas, WPP Plc's Ogilvy & Mather and Cordiant Plc's Saatchi & Saatchi.

PARIS - McCann Erickson Paris says its parent, U.S. advertising agency McCann Erickson Worldwide, has won the worldwide advertising campaign for throat lozenges Strepsils which was previously run by DDB Worldwide. The advertising budget for Strepsils is about 160 million francs ($27.7 million) this year across the 110 countries where the product is sold.

FRANKFURT - Advertising agency J. Walter Thompson's German unit posts record 1996 sales and predicts more growth this year. Turnover in 1996 rose by 7.4 percent to 85 million marks ($49.8 million) while billings climbed by 7.6 percent to 566 million marks.

LONDON - Microsoft Corp, the U.S. software giant fighting for share in the crowded Internet service provider market, says it plans to launch an aggressive new multi-million pound UK advertising campaign.
PARIS - Canal Plus launches Canal Regie Internationale, an agency which will place advertising with television channels broadcast outside France.

LONDON - Olympic gold medal winner, Marie-Jose Perec from France, stars in a new, global advertising campaign launched by Pirelli, the Italian tyre-maker. It will run in Europe, the United States, Latin America and Asia. Details of the ad budget are not disclosed.
MEDIA AND THE INTERNET:

LONDON - British radio operator GWR Group Plc says its Classic FM unit is part of a consortium awarded one of three new FM licences in greater Johannesburg, South Africa. GWR says Classic will own a 20 percent stake in the station in return for supplying show formats, musical databases, training and advice on programming and marketing.
TOKYO - Softbank Corp, Sony Corp and News Corp will formally decide on their investment stakes in Japan Sky Broadcasting by the end of this month, the Jiji news agency says.

PARIS - French media group Havas would like an Anglo-Saxon shareholder to bolster its presence on the other side of the Atlantic, chairman Pierre Dauzier says. But he says the group is in no hurry and adds that it will remain a key shareholder in Havas Advertising.

NEW YORK - CMG Information Services Inc is expected to go on-line with a service linking 39 Internet access providers in a pool for advertisers according to a newspaper report. The service, Planet Direct, targets advertisers interested in reaching 560,000 subscribers served by access providers.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS AND MARKETS:
SHANGHAI - McDonald's Corp plans to open 11 more restaurants in Shanghai this year, bringing the number of its outlets in China's largest city to 28, the China Daily Business Weekly says.
TOKYO - Akai Electric Co Ltd, a Tokyo-based audio equipment maker, says it has agreed to sponsor the Benetton Formula One team in the 1997 and 1998 seasons.

CLEVELAND - Several U.S. retailers who import Asian goods through Hong Kong say they expect little impact when the British colony reverts to Chinese rule this summer. J.C. Penney Co. Inc. and Federated Department Stores Inc. say they foresee no supply problems during or after the hand over and plan no changes in the routes they use to import goods.

BEIJING - General Motors Corp appears to be closing in on its $1.0 billion China car joint venture, with a deal expected to be signed soon. It will have the capacity to build about 100,000 vehicles a year.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

CHICAGO - Bagel sales continue to heat up across the U.S. Sales in 1996 were an estimated $2.3 billion, up from $1.6 billion in 1995 and only $429 million in 1993, according to the Independent Bakers Association.

NEW YORK - Forget the much-hyped burger war between McDonald's and Burger King. The looming threat isn't each other -- it's the sudden rise of chicken on the fast food scene. It appeals to working people who don't have time to prepare meals and has more of a home-cooked look and flavour than hamburgers and fries, say industry experts.

CHICAGO - China's consumers are becoming more affluent and sophisticated, but their preferences and dislikes are vastly different from their American counterparts, says a study by ad agency Leo Burnett. The Chinese have a much deeper interest in health issues than Americans and maintaining a clean home at all times is very important to 94 percent of Chinese consumers, but to only 49 percent of U.S. consumers.
SOFIA - Bulgarian scientists have used cloning techniques to develop tobacco strains that are resistant to disease, pests and environmental stress. They are now looking for markets for the product.
